classification.difficultyReason: Introduce root sum and product, eliminate the product between two power-sum conditions, solve the resulting cubic, and retain every real coefficient pair without imposing real-root restrictions.

content.prompt: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the roots of the monic quadratic equation $x^2+px+q=0$. Given that $\alpha^2+\beta^2=6$ and $\alpha^3+\beta^3=4$, find all real coefficient pairs $(p,q)$. The roots themselves need not be real.

answer.short:
$(p,q)=(-4,5)$, $(2-\sqrt6,\ 2-2\sqrt6)$ or $(2+\sqrt6,\ 2+2\sqrt6)$.

Set $S=\alpha+\beta$ and use the two power sums to factorise a cubic in $S$.
answer.worked:
Let $S=\alpha+\beta$ and $P=\alpha\beta$.
$$\begin{align*}S^2-2P&=6\\P&=\frac{S^2-6}{2}.\end{align*}$$
Also $\alpha^3+\beta^3=S^3-3PS=4$. Substituting gives
$$\begin{align*}S^3-\frac{3S(S^2-6)}2&=4\\S^3-18S+8&=0\\(S-4)(S^2+4S-2)&=0.\end{align*}$$
The factor theorem and quadratic formula give $S=4$ or $S=-2\pm\sqrt6$. Since $p=-S$ and $q=P$,
$$\begin{array}{c|c|c}S&p&q\\\hline 4&-4&5\\-2+\sqrt6&2-\sqrt6&2-2\sqrt6\\-2-\sqrt6&2+\sqrt6&2+2\sqrt6\end{array}$$
Each pair satisfies both power sums. The question permits non-real roots, so all three real coefficient pairs are retained.
